lessons.claim: A pre-registered decision rule that rests a verdict on STATIONARITY is weaker than one that rests it on CONVERGENCE, and the difference is not visible until the data exists. Measured: two arms started at competing candidate profiles, 1/3 seeds stationary in each (0.6 sigma apart, no signal), so the sealed rule returned INCONCLUSIVE -- while the same data showed four different starting conditions converging to one state, agreeing with one candidate at 1.8 sigma and rejecting the other at 4.5-18 sigma. Stationarity can only say 'nothing moved us'; convergence says 'four starting points arrive here'. Register the convergence branch as a route to a verdict, not as a failure mode.
